reading.body:
Troy Balderson's AI record is mostly money: 11 of 17 dated events are contributions from AI and chip company PACs, and every one of his four recorded votes was Yea.

The contributions run from March 2025 to August 2026 and come from Amazon, Intel, Google, Meta, Oracle, and Anthropic's PAC. Individual amounts are small, between $1,000 and $5,000, and one Meta entry is a $2,000 contribution reversed the next day. The donors are the companies that build and host AI systems, so the money tracks the compute supply chain rather than AI users or researchers.

The four votes are on H.R. 7757, H.R. 5764, H.R. 1770, and S. 146, all passed under suspension of the rules. The data does not say what any of these bills do, so it cannot show whether they touch AI, data centers, or grid policy. It also does not establish that any contribution influenced any vote, and the page states that placement in date order is not a claim of causation.

What the record does not contain is as notable as what it does. There are no sponsored bills listed, no committee assignments, no letters or statements, and no contributions from utilities, power developers, or grid equipment makers. On this data, Balderson reads as a recipient of AI industry PAC money and a reliable yes on suspended bills, not as a legislator whose AI or energy positions can be characterized.
